title: Pressure injury stages

findings.where: Images 1–6 and 9–14; Stage 3 wound bed; pressure-injury.jsx Slough
findings.title: The apparent fat landmark is actually unlabeled slough
findings.problem: The conspicuous yellow-brown patch in the Stage 3 wound is coded as slough, but nothing labels it. Beside text emphasizing 'fat visible' and a similarly colored fat legend, students can reasonably identify that patch as exposed fat. The smooth coral bed does not otherwise distinguish exposed adipose from the Stage 2 bed.
findings.fix: Label the patch 'slough' with a leader. Depict identifiable lobulated adipose along an exposed portion of the Stage 3 wound bed or wall, separately from the slough.

findings.where: Images 1–6 and 9–14; tissue bands and legend; LAYERS and legend rendering
findings.title: The layer key does not provide an accessible match to the tissue bands
findings.problem: The bands have distinct textures, but the legend swatches omit those textures and supply no leaders or matching identifiers. Matching therefore relies primarily on low-contrast fills. Epidermis and dermis are especially difficult to separate in dark mode: their composited fills differ by only about 1.2:1, and the thin boundary line does not provide a strong alternative.
findings.fix: Repeat each tissue texture in its legend swatch and add direct labels, leaders, or matching identifiers. Strengthen the essential layer boundaries in both themes rather than relying on subtle tint differences.

assessment: Revise the Stage 3 illustration and tissue-layer key before publication.
